title: MM-MT106-ModelToModelPolicy

scope.summary:
GOAL: The deny-by-default policy layer for model-to-model orchestration: WHICH parent roles/sessions may spawn WHICH lanes/roles, per-parent concurrent-children cap, per-parent budget ceiling, allowed workspace modes, and steer/interrupt capability flags. Policy rows are versioned and ledgered; the operator has an override surface (config + API). MT-101 defines the evaluator trait (co-designed); this MT ships the real config-backed, PG-versioned implementation that MT-101 (spawn) and MT-102 (steer/interrupt) handlers evaluate.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/m2m_policy/ (mod.rs + rules.rs + store.rs + evaluator.rs); one new numbered migration pair for `m2m_policy_rules` (versioned rows) and `m2m_policy_decisions` is NOT a table (decisions go to the process_ledger like every other action); config schema additions under `model_to_model.policy.*`; an operator-facing HTTP API surface (list/get/put rules) following the existing handshake_core API router conventions; registration of the evaluator into the MT-101 model_tools registry at startup. Tests.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Rule shape (rules.rs): `M2mPolicyRule { rule_id, version, parent_selector (role_id | session_id | any), child_role_selector (role_id | any), allowed_lanes: [lane ids validated against ModelLaneStore], allowed_workspace_modes: [worktree|worktree_vm|none], max_concurrent_children: u32, budget_ceiling { max_child_tokens?, max_child_cost?, max_child_wall_secs? }, may_steer: bool, may_interrupt: bool, orphan_on_parent_termination_allowed: bool, enabled: bool, created_by, created_at_utc }`. Selectors resolve against the MT-081/MT-086 role registry.
2. Deny-by-default: evaluation with zero matching enabled rules = DENY. Rule matching is most-specific-wins (session > role > any); ties broken by newest version; a matching rule with enabled=false is an explicit deny that shadows broader allows.
3. Versioning + ledgering: rules are immutable rows — every change inserts a new version, never updates in place; the store answers `rules_as_of(timestamp)` so any past decision is re-derivable. Every rule change writes a process_ledger row (who, what changed, old/new version). Every EVALUATION (allow and deny) is ledgered by the calling handler with the rule_id+version that decided it (MT-101/102 obligation, restated here).
4. Evaluator (evaluator.rs): implements the MT-101 trait: `evaluate_spawn(parent_ctx, SpawnWorkerInput) -> PolicyDecision`, `evaluate_steer(parent_ctx, child_ctx, kind: steer|interrupt) -> PolicyDecision`. PolicyDecision carries decision, rule_id, version, denial reason enum (NoMatchingRule, RoleNotAllowed, LaneNotAllowed, WorkspaceModeNotAllowed, ConcurrentChildrenCapReached, BudgetCeilingExceeded, SteerNotAllowed, InterruptNotAllowed, RuleDisabled). Concurrent-children counting reads MT-103 live lineage.
5. Operator override surface: (a) config file layer — `model_to_model.policy.rules` seeds baseline rules at startup (seed = insert-if-absent by rule_id, versioned like any change); (b) HTTP API — GET /m2m/policy/rules, GET /m2m/policy/rules/{rule_id}, PUT /m2m/policy/rules/{rule_id} (inserts new version); API is operator-plane only (same auth posture as other operator config APIs), NEVER exposed as a model tool. A kill switch `model_to_model.policy.global_disable` forces DENY for all model-initiated spawn/steer instantly.
6. Budget ceiling semantics: the ceiling CLAMPS requested budgets in MT-101 (grant = min(request, ceiling)); ConcurrentChildrenCapReached is evaluated against live children count at spawn time; the policy cap is per-parent and sits UNDER the coordinator's global semaphore/lifetime caps — policy can only narrow, never widen, coordinator enforcement.

SECURITY FRAME (binding): this is the authorization brain of the privilege-escalation surface. No model-facing write path to rules may exist; the evaluator fails CLOSED (store error => DENY, ledgered); policy narrows but never bypasses SwarmCoordinator caps/ceilings/leases/consent gates.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the MT-101 evaluator trait, MT-103 lineage queries, model_lane.rs lane ids, role registry seam (MT-081/086), existing API router + migration conventions.
2. Author migration for m2m_policy_rules (immutable versioned rows, indexes on selectors + enabled).
3. Implement rules.rs types + matching (most-specific-wins, explicit-deny shadowing) and store.rs (insert-new-version, rules_as_of, seed-from-config).
4. Implement evaluator.rs with fail-closed store-error handling and live concurrent-children counting.
5. Implement the operator HTTP API (list/get/put) + global_disable kill switch.
6. Register evaluator at startup; tests per expected_tests.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/** (next free numeric prefix only; paired .down.sql)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/** (operator policy routes only, following existing router conventions)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs (policy narrows under coordinator caps; coordinator is untouched)
acceptance_criteria: m2m_policy_rules migration (up+down) green on managed PostgreSQL; rows are immutable versions (no UPDATE path in the store).
Deny-by-default proven: zero matching rules => DENY(NoMatchingRule); disabled matching rule shadows broader allows.
Most-specific-wins matching (session > role > any, newest version tiebreak) covered by unit tests across the selector matrix.

Evaluator enforces: role/lane/workspace-mode allowlists, per-parent concurrent-children cap (counted from MT-103 live lineage), budget ceiling clamp, may_steer/may_interrupt flags — each with a typed denial reason.
Store/database error during evaluation fails CLOSED (DENY, ledgered with error class); fault-injection test proves no fail-open.
Every rule change is a new ledgered version; rules_as_of(t) reproduces historical rule sets.

Operator API list/get/put works, is operator-plane only, and is NOT registered on any model tool channel (negative test); PUT inserts a new version and takes effect on next evaluation without restart.
model_to_model.policy.global_disable kill switch forces DENY for all model-initiated spawn/steer immediately.
Policy caps sit under coordinator caps: a policy allowing more than the coordinator's global limits still hits coordinator rejection (integration test documents the layering).
expected_tests: unit: selector matrix (session/role/any x allow/deny/disabled) most-specific-wins outcomes
unit: budget clamp math and each typed denial reason
integration (managed PG): versioned insert, rules_as_of reproduction, seed-from-config idempotency
integration: evaluator wired into MT-101 spawn handler — allowed spawn passes, each denial reason reachable
negative: model tool channel does not expose policy read/write; kill switch forces DENY
implementation_notes: Policy decisions are ledger rows, not a decisions table: reuse the process_ledger like every other governed action to keep one audit spine.
Seeding from config must be idempotent and versioned so a config edit + restart produces exactly one new version per changed rule, not duplicates.

Selector resolution against the role registry (MT-081/086) should tolerate unknown role ids in rules with a typed validation warning at load (rule inert until the role exists) rather than crashing startup.
The layering statement matters for audits: coordinator caps are the hard outer wall (unchangeable by policy); m2m policy is the narrower inner wall an operator tunes.
Operator GUI for policy editing is future work (the API is the contract surface); MT-107 GUI shows decisions, not rule editing.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-081/086 role registry, MT-101/102 evaluation call sites, MT-103 lineage counting.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Policy engine + operator HTTP API only; no GUI in this MT (MT-107 renders decisions; rule-editing GUI is future scope).

target_entries: Model-to-model orchestration: policy rules — deny-by-default, rule shape and selectors, per-parent caps and budget ceilings, operator API (list/get/put), config seeding, global_disable kill switch

risk_if_missed: Spawn/steer tools ship with only a stub gate: either everything is denied (feature dead) or an improvised allow-all leaks in — model-initiated spawning without operator-tunable authorization, unbounded per-parent fan-out under the global caps, and no audit trail of who allowed what.

risks: RISK-1: Fail-open evaluation — a store error, unknown selector, or matching bug returns ALLOW, converting the authorization brain into a rubber stamp.
RISK-2: Model-reachable policy writes — a policy mutation surface leaks onto a model tool channel and a model rewrites its own permissions (self-escalation).
RISK-3: Rule-shadowing confusion — overlapping rules resolve differently than the operator expects (broad allow beats specific deny), granting unintended spawn authority.
RISK-4: Unauditable history — in-place rule updates destroy the record of what was allowed when, making past spawn decisions unexplainable.
RISK-5: TOCTOU on concurrent-children cap — two simultaneous spawns both read count=cap-1 and both pass, exceeding the per-parent cap.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Fail-closed contract on every error path (store error, unknown role, matcher panic => DENY ledgered); fault-injection test.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Policy API lives on the operator plane only; negative test asserts no policy tool on the model channel; MT-101/102 handlers hold only the read-side evaluator.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Deterministic most-specific-wins with explicit-deny shadowing, fully covered by a selector-matrix unit test; the manual documents the resolution order.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Immutable versioned rows + rules_as_of + ledgered changes; no UPDATE path exists in the store.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Cap check performed atomically (transactional count+reserve or serialized per-parent lock) with a concurrency test spawning in parallel at the cap boundary; coordinator global caps remain the hard outer bound either way.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: model_lane.rs (lane ids, ModelLaneAuthority/RoutingPolicy precedent for policy enums), mcp/gate.rs (deny-by-default gate decision precedent: evaluate_kernel_tool_gate_decision), migrations/ conventions, process_ledger/ (single audit spine). External precedent: RBAC most-specific-wins with explicit-deny (cloud IAM conventions), immutable versioned policy rows (policy-as-data audit practice), kill-switch pattern for agent authorization layers.
